{
  "root_cause": "The focus trap fails because the active element (#upload) is not found in the array returned by getFocusableNodes(), causing indexOf to return -1. Consequently, the wrap‑around conditions in maintainFocus are not met, event.preventDefault() is not called, and focus leaves the modal to the next focusable element in the document (the help link).",
  "repair_strategy": "Update the maintainFocus method in the micromodal library to robustly handle cases where the active element is not present in the focusable nodes list. Treat such a situation as an exit from the modal and wrap focus to the appropriate end (first for Tab, last for Shift+Tab) while guarding against empty node lists.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Keyboard focus will remain confined to the modal dialog when tabbing forward or backward, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). Users will be able to cycle through the filename input, upload button, and close button without escaping to page elements outside the modal.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "The modified focus trap could interfere with custom focus management if other scripts rely on the original behavior.",
    "If the modal contains no focusable nodes, the early return prevents errors but may leave focus unchanged.",
    "Changes to focus handling must not break the existing Escape‑to‑close functionality or the upload button's action."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that tabbing forward from the filename input moves focus to the upload button, then to the close button, then back to the filename input.",
    "Verify that shift+tabbing backward cycles in the reverse order.",
    "Confirm that pressing Escape closes the modal and returns focus to the trigger button.",
    "Ensure the upload button still updates the status text correctly.",
    "Check that background page scrolling remains disabled while the modal is open (if applicable)."
  ]
}
